```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Bousema et al. (2010) fitted two simple deterministic compartmental models
to Pfs25 QT-NASBA gametocyte data from two antimalarial trials in East
African children, each trial separately:

* a **density model** -- sequestered gametocytes `S` are released into the
  circulation at rate `rho`, and circulating gametocytes `G` decay at rate
  `mu`, so that `1 / mu` is the mean circulation time of a gametocyte;
* a **prevalence model** -- a gametocyte-negative patient `E` becomes
  gametocyte-positive `I` at rate `f`, and a positive patient clears
  gametocytes at rate `r`, so that `1 / r` is the mean duration of
  gametocyte carriage.

The treatment arms enter as arm-specific circulation times, day-3 densities
and durations of carriage. The paper's four fits are packaged as four model
files:

| Model | Trial | Arms (indicator) |
|---|---|---|
| `Bousema_2010_malaria_gametocyte_density_kenya` | Kenya 2003-2004 | non-ACT (reference) / ACT (`TRT_ARTEMISININ`) |
| `Bousema_2010_malaria_gametocyte_density_tanzania` | Tanzania 2006 | ACT (reference) / ACT + primaquine (`TRT_PRIMAQUINE`) |
| `Bousema_2010_malaria_gametocyte_prevalence_kenya` | Kenya 2003-2004 | non-ACT / ACT (`TRT_ARTEMISININ`) |
| `Bousema_2010_malaria_gametocyte_prevalence_tanzania` | Tanzania 2006 | ACT / ACT + primaquine (`TRT_PRIMAQUINE`) |

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Bousema_2010_malaria_gametocyte_density_kenya"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1186/1475-2875-9-136> (open access)
* Additional file 1 (sensitivity of the circulation time to the size of the
  sequestered pool): published with the article.

**Time origin.** The density models describe the second phase of carriage
only, after the drugs' direct effect has waned: their time zero is **day 3
after the start of treatment**, and their initial states are the day-3
densities. The prevalence models start at the start of treatment (day 0).

# Population

The Kenya trial (Mbita, 2003-2004, about 70 infectious bites per person per
year) enrolled children aged 0.5-10 years (median 3) with uncomplicated
falciparum malaria; 36 children treated with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine +
amodiaquine (non-ACT) and 90 treated with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine +
artesunate or artemether-lumefantrine (ACT, pooled) entered the model fits.
The Tanzania trial (Mnyuzi, 2006, about 10 infectious bites per person per
year) enrolled children aged 3-15 years (median 5); 36 children treated with
sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine + artesunate (ACT) and 41 treated with the same ACT
plus a single 0.75 mg/kg primaquine dose on the third treatment day (ACT-PQ)
entered the fits (Bousema 2010 Table 1). Only children cured of asexual
parasites without re-infection and gametocyte-positive by QT-NASBA at least
once between day 0 and day 28 were included; weight and sex were not
reported.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Bousema_2010_malaria_gametocyte_density_kenya")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. They are
collected here.

| Model / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Density ODEs `dS/dt = -rho S`, `dG/dt = rho S - mu G` | -- | Methods, first density-model equation |
| Density closed form `G(t)` | -- | Methods, second density-model equation (checked below) |
| Prevalence ODEs `dE/dt = -f E`, `dI/dt = f E - r I` | -- | Methods, first prevalence-model equation |
| Prevalence closed form `I(t)` | -- | Methods, second prevalence-model equation (checked below) |
| `lmst` (both density models) | log(11) day, fixed | Table 2 `1/rho` = 1/11; Methods (best fit within 4-12 days) |
| Kenya `lmct_nonact` | log(6.53) day | Figure 2 caption 6.53 (4.84-8.80); Results 6.5 |
| Kenya `lmct_act` | log(5.04) day | Figure 2 caption 5.04 (4.20-6.06); Results 5.0 |
| Kenya `lg3_nonact` | log(1.45) /uL | Table 2 G3 non-ACT 1.45 (0.44-4.74) |
| Kenya `lg3_act` | log(0.13) /uL | Table 2 G3 ACT 0.13 (0.03-0.52) |
| Kenya `ls3_nonact` | log(0.0263) /uL, fixed | Table 2 S3; Additional file 1 best-fit row (ln -3.64) |
| Kenya `ls3_act` | log(0.0263) - 3, fixed | Methods ('3 log lower'); Table 2 S3 ACT 0.0013 (ln -6.64) |
| Tanzania `lmct_act` | log(4.61) day | Figure 3 caption 4.61 (2.92-7.26); Results 4.6 |
| Tanzania `lmct_actpq` | log(0.53) day | Figure 3 caption 0.53 (0.24-1.19); Results 0.5 |
| Tanzania `lg3_act` | log(1.88) /uL | Table 2 G3 ACT 1.88 (0.37-9.52) |
| Tanzania `lg3_actpq` | log(0.07) /uL | Table 2 G3 ACT-PQ 0.07 (0.01-0.86) |
| Tanzania `ls3` | log(0.0013) /uL | Table 2 S3 0.0013 (0.0001-0.0237) |
| Kenya `lmtpos` | log(5.60) day | Table 2 `1/f` 5.60 (1.06-29.4), estimated in the Kenya trial |
| Tanzania `lmtpos` | log(5.60) day, fixed | Table 2 `1/f` footnote: estimated from the Kenya data |
| Kenya `lmdur_nonact` | log(55.6) day | Table 3 55.6 (28.7-107.7); Figure 4 caption |
| Kenya `lmdur_act` | log(13.4) day | Table 3 13.4 (10.2-17.5); Figure 4 caption |
| Tanzania `lmdur_act` | log(28.6) day | Table 3 28.6 (17.0-48.0); Figure 5 caption |
| Tanzania `lmdur_actpq` | log(6.3) day | Table 3 6.3 (4.7-8.5); Figure 5 caption |
| `etalg3`, `expSd`, `etalogitgam` | 0, fixed | Methods name these random effects; their variances are not reported |

Units of every ODE term:

| Term | Units |
|---|---|
| `gametocyte_sequestered`, `gametocyte_circulating` (S, G) | gametocytes per uL blood |
| `rho * S`, `mu * G` | gametocytes per uL per day |
| `s_gametocyteneg`, `s_gametocytepos` (E, I) | probability (unitless) |
| `f * E`, `I * r` | probability per day |

# Load the models

```{r load}
mod_dk <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Bousema_2010_malaria_gametocyte_density_kenya"))
mod_dt <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Bousema_2010_malaria_gametocyte_density_tanzania"))
mod_pk <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Bousema_2010_malaria_gametocyte_prevalence_kenya"))
mod_pt <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Bousema_2010_malaria_gametocyte_prevalence_tanzania"))
```

The random-effect variances and the residual SD are not reported, so the
models carry them as `fixed(0)`; the simulations below are typical-value
solves.

# Density model

## Typical-value solve and the published closed form

One typical patient per arm is solved on a daily grid from day 3 to day 28
after the start of treatment (model time 0 to 25). The solve is checked
against the paper's closed-form solution
`G(t) = exp(-mu t) G0 + rho S0 (exp(-mu t) - exp(-rho t)) / (rho - mu)`.

```{r density-solve}
model_days <- seq(0, 25, by = 0.25)

# One typical patient per solve: with every random effect fixed at zero,
# rxode2 warns about a multi-subject simulation without omega.
dens_solve <- function(mod, trt_col, trt_value) {
  ev <- data.frame(time = model_days, evid = 0, cmt = "gametocyte_circulating")
  ev[[trt_col]] <- trt_value
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev))
}

sim_dk <- bind_rows(
  dens_solve(mod_dk, "TRT_ARTEMISININ", 0) |> mutate(arm = "non-ACT"),
  dens_solve(mod_dk, "TRT_ARTEMISININ", 1) |> mutate(arm = "ACT")
) |>
  mutate(trial = "Kenya")
sim_dt <- bind_rows(
  dens_solve(mod_dt, "TRT_PRIMAQUINE", 0) |> mutate(arm = "ACT"),
  dens_solve(mod_dt, "TRT_PRIMAQUINE", 1) |> mutate(arm = "ACT-PQ")
) |>
  mutate(trial = "Tanzania")

dens_par <- tribble(
  ~trial,     ~arm,      ~g3,   ~s3,                 ~mct,
  "Kenya",    "non-ACT", 1.45,  0.0263,              6.53,
  "Kenya",    "ACT",     0.13,  exp(log(0.0263) - 3), 5.04,
  "Tanzania", "ACT",     1.88,  0.0013,              4.61,
  "Tanzania", "ACT-PQ",  0.07,  0.0013,              0.53
)

dens_sim <- bind_rows(sim_dk, sim_dt) |>
  select(trial, arm, time, gametocyte_density) |>
  left_join(dens_par, by = c("trial", "arm")) |>
  mutate(
    rho = 1 / 11,
    mu = 1 / mct,
    closed_form = exp(-mu * time) * g3 +
      rho * s3 * (exp(-mu * time) - exp(-rho * time)) / (rho - mu),
    rel_diff = abs(gametocyte_density - closed_form) / closed_form,
    day = time + 3
  )

# The ODE solve and the closed form use the same parameters, so they agree
# to solver tolerance.
stopifnot(max(dens_sim$rel_diff) < 1e-4)
max(dens_sim$rel_diff)
```

At late times the circulating density decays at close to `mu`, so the
slope of log density against time between days 14 and 28 recovers the
published mean circulation time to within a few percent (the slow release
of the sequestered pool flattens it slightly):

```{r density-slope}
dens_sim |>
  filter(day %in% c(14, 28)) |>
  group_by(trial, arm) |>
  summarise(
    published_mct = first(mct),
    slope_mct = -(28 - 14) / diff(log(gametocyte_density)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

The ACT-PQ arm is the exception: its circulating pool is gone within days
and the density thereafter tracks the slow release of the small sequestered
pool (`1 / rho` = 11 days), as the paper describes for Figure 3.

## Comparison with Figures 2 and 3

The fitted lines of Figures 2 and 3 were digitised by the maintainers at the
sampling days (natural-log density; the plots' dotted detection limit,
0.02 gametocytes/uL, sits at about -3.8).

```{r density-figure, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
fig_dens <- tribble(
  ~trial,     ~arm,      ~day, ~published_line,
  "Kenya",    "non-ACT",  3,    0.643,
  "Kenya",    "non-ACT",  7,    0.136,
  "Kenya",    "non-ACT", 14,   -0.724,
  "Kenya",    "non-ACT", 28,   -2.077,
  "Kenya",    "ACT",      3,   -1.290,
  "Kenya",    "ACT",      7,   -1.788,
  "Kenya",    "ACT",     14,   -2.541,
  "Kenya",    "ACT",     28,   -3.509,
  "Tanzania", "ACT",      3,    1.372,
  "Tanzania", "ACT",      7,    0.626,
  "Tanzania", "ACT",     14,   -0.379,
  "Tanzania", "ACT",     28,   -1.981,
  "Tanzania", "ACT-PQ",   3,   -0.910,
  "Tanzania", "ACT-PQ",   7,   -3.378,
  "Tanzania", "ACT-PQ",  14,   -3.709,
  "Tanzania", "ACT-PQ",  28,   -3.714
)

dens_cmp <- fig_dens |>
  left_join(
    dens_sim |> select(trial, arm, day, gametocyte_density),
    by = c("trial", "arm", "day")
  ) |>
  mutate(model_log_typical = log(gametocyte_density))

dens_cmp |>
  select(trial, arm, day, published_line, model_log_typical) |>
  rename(
    "Trial" = trial, "Arm" = arm, "Day" = day,
    "Published fitted line, ln(G)" = published_line,
    "Model typical value, ln(G)" = model_log_typical
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

ggplot(dens_sim, aes(day, log(gametocyte_density), colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = dens_cmp, aes(y = published_line), shape = 1, size = 2.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = log(0.02), linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~trial) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-8, 3)) +
  labs(
    x = "Days since start of treatment",
    y = "ln gametocyte density (/uL)",
    colour = "Arm",
    caption = "Lines: model typical value. Circles: fitted lines digitised from Figures 2 and 3."
  )
```

At day 3 the model's typical density sits 0.3-0.8 natural-log units below
the published lines (1.8 for ACT-PQ), and the published lines decline more
slowly than `exp(-mu t)`: from day 3 to day 28 the Kenya non-ACT line falls
`r with(dens_cmp, round(published_line[arm == "non-ACT" & day == 3] - published_line[arm == "non-ACT" & day == 28], 1))`
natural-log units where the model falls
`r with(dens_cmp, round(model_log_typical[arm == "non-ACT" & day == 3] - model_log_typical[arm == "non-ACT" & day == 28], 1))`. The lines are
therefore not the typical-value curve `ln G(t)` at the Table 2 estimates.
They are consistent in direction with the expected value of a log-normal
observation left-censored at the detection limit -- the lines flatten as
they approach it, and the ACT-PQ line runs along it -- but the random-effect
and residual variances needed to compute that expectation are not reported,
so the figures cannot be reproduced exactly. The circulation times, which
are the paper's headline result, are carried by the packaged rates (see the
slope table above).

# Prevalence model

## Typical-value solve and the published closed form

The paper's closed form
`I(t) = exp(-r t) I0 + f (1 - I0) (exp(-r t) - exp(-f t)) / (f - r)` is the
prevalence in a cohort whose fraction `I0` is positive at day 0. In the
packaged model `I0` is the patient's enrolment status `GAMETOCYTE_POS_BASE`;
averaging the patient-level solve over a cohort gives the closed form, which
is checked here with a virtual cohort per arm built from the enrolment
gametocyte-negative counts in the Table 2 footnote.

```{r prevalence-cohort}
cohort <- tribble(
  ~trial,     ~arm,      ~n, ~n_neg,
  "Kenya",    "non-ACT", 36,  4,
  "Kenya",    "ACT",     90, 12,
  "Tanzania", "ACT",     36,  6,
  "Tanzania", "ACT-PQ",  41,  4
) |>
  mutate(I0 = 1 - n_neg / n)

prev_days <- seq(0, 28, by = 0.5)

prev_events <- function(trial_name, trt_col) {
  arms <- cohort |> filter(trial == trial_name) |> mutate(trt = row_number() - 1)
  subj <- arms |>
    group_by(arm, trt) |>
    reframe(GAMETOCYTE_POS_BASE = rep(c(0, 1), c(n_neg, n - n_neg))) |>
    mutate(id = row_number())
  expand.grid(time = prev_days, id = subj$id) |>
    left_join(subj, by = "id") |>
    mutate(evid = 0, cmt = "s_gametocytepos", !!trt_col := trt)
}

sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pk, which = "omega"), prev_events("Kenya", "TRT_ARTEMISININ"),
  keep = c("arm", "GAMETOCYTE_POS_BASE")
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(trial = "Kenya")
sim_pt <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pt, which = "omega"), prev_events("Tanzania", "TRT_PRIMAQUINE"),
  keep = c("arm", "GAMETOCYTE_POS_BASE")
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(trial = "Tanzania")

prev_par <- tribble(
  ~trial,     ~arm,      ~dur,
  "Kenya",    "non-ACT", 55.6,
  "Kenya",    "ACT",     13.4,
  "Tanzania", "ACT",     28.6,
  "Tanzania", "ACT-PQ",  6.3
)

prev_cohort <- bind_rows(sim_pk, sim_pt) |>
  group_by(trial, arm, time) |>
  summarise(prevalence = mean(p_gametocytepos), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(prev_par, by = c("trial", "arm")) |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(trial, arm, I0), by = c("trial", "arm")) |>
  mutate(
    f = 1 / 5.60,
    r = 1 / dur,
    closed_form = exp(-r * time) * I0 +
      f * (1 - I0) * (exp(-r * time) - exp(-f * time)) / (f - r)
  )

stopifnot(max(abs(prev_cohort$prevalence - prev_cohort$closed_form)) < 1e-5)
max(abs(prev_cohort$prevalence - prev_cohort$closed_form))
```

## Mean duration of carriage

For a patient who is gametocyte-positive at enrolment, the expected time
spent gametocyte-positive is the area under `s_gametocytepos`, which must
equal `1 / r` -- the duration of carriage in Table 3.

```{r duration}
long_days <- seq(0, 1500, by = 0.5)
dur_check <- bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pk, which = "omega"),
    data.frame(id = rep(1:2, each = length(long_days)), time = long_days, evid = 0,
      cmt = "s_gametocytepos", TRT_ARTEMISININ = rep(c(0, 1), each = length(long_days)),
      GAMETOCYTE_POS_BASE = 1)
  ) |> as.data.frame() |> mutate(trial = "Kenya", arm = ifelse(id == 1, "non-ACT", "ACT")),
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pt, which = "omega"),
    data.frame(id = rep(1:2, each = length(long_days)), time = long_days, evid = 0,
      cmt = "s_gametocytepos", TRT_PRIMAQUINE = rep(c(0, 1), each = length(long_days)),
      GAMETOCYTE_POS_BASE = 1)
  ) |> as.data.frame() |> mutate(trial = "Tanzania", arm = ifelse(id == 1, "ACT", "ACT-PQ"))
) |>
  group_by(trial, arm) |>
  summarise(
    simulated_duration = sum(diff(time) * (head(s_gametocytepos, -1) + tail(s_gametocytepos, -1)) / 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(prev_par, by = c("trial", "arm")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated_duration - dur) / dur)

dur_check |>
  rename(
    "Trial" = trial, "Arm" = arm,
    "Area under P(positive), days" = simulated_duration,
    "Table 3 duration, days" = dur,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# Trapezoidal integration of a smooth exponential on a 0.5-day grid.
stopifnot(max(abs(dur_check$pct_diff)) < 0.1)
```

The fourfold reductions the paper reports follow directly: non-ACT to ACT
in Kenya `r round(55.6 / 13.4, 1)`-fold, ACT to ACT-PQ in Tanzania
`r round(28.6 / 6.3, 1)`-fold.

## Comparison with Figures 4 and 5 and Table 3

The fitted lines of Figures 4 and 5 were digitised by the maintainers at the
sampling days. Those lines are the paper's *marginal* predictions: 10,000
draws of the patient random effect added on the logit scale and averaged.
The typical-value prediction is computed here with `I0` set to each line's
digitised day-0 value.

```{r prevalence-figure, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
fig_prev <- tribble(
  ~trial,     ~arm,      ~time, ~published_line,
  "Kenya",    "non-ACT",  0,    0.903,
  "Kenya",    "non-ACT",  3,    0.854,
  "Kenya",    "non-ACT",  7,    0.787,
  "Kenya",    "non-ACT", 14,    0.703,
  "Kenya",    "non-ACT", 28,    0.570,
  "Kenya",    "ACT",      0,    0.893,
  "Kenya",    "ACT",      3,    0.706,
  "Kenya",    "ACT",      7,    0.564,
  "Kenya",    "ACT",     14,    0.396,
  "Kenya",    "ACT",     28,    0.200,
  "Tanzania", "ACT",      0,    0.985,
  "Tanzania", "ACT",      3,    0.851,
  "Tanzania", "ACT",      7,    0.725,
  "Tanzania", "ACT",     14,    0.580,
  "Tanzania", "ACT",     28,    0.401,
  "Tanzania", "ACT-PQ",   0,    0.984,
  "Tanzania", "ACT-PQ",   3,    0.585,
  "Tanzania", "ACT-PQ",   7,    0.362,
  "Tanzania", "ACT-PQ",  14,    0.157,
  "Tanzania", "ACT-PQ",  28,    0.020
)

i0_fig <- fig_prev |> filter(time == 0) |> select(trial, arm, I0_fig = published_line)

fig_events <- bind_rows(
  expand.grid(time = prev_days, id = 1:2) |>
    mutate(trial = "Kenya", TRT_ARTEMISININ = id - 1, arm = ifelse(id == 1, "non-ACT", "ACT")),
  expand.grid(time = prev_days, id = 3:4) |>
    mutate(trial = "Tanzania", TRT_PRIMAQUINE = id - 3, arm = ifelse(id == 3, "ACT", "ACT-PQ"))
) |>
  left_join(i0_fig, by = c("trial", "arm")) |>
  mutate(evid = 0, cmt = "s_gametocytepos", GAMETOCYTE_POS_BASE = I0_fig) |>
  arrange(id, time)

prev_fig_sim <- bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pk, which = "omega"), filter(fig_events, trial == "Kenya") |> select(-TRT_PRIMAQUINE),
    keep = c("trial", "arm")
  ) |> as.data.frame(),
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pt, which = "omega"), filter(fig_events, trial == "Tanzania") |> select(-TRT_ARTEMISININ),
    keep = c("trial", "arm")
  ) |> as.data.frame()
)

table3 <- tribble(
  ~trial,     ~arm,      ~time, ~observed,
  "Kenya",    "non-ACT", 14,    28 / 36,
  "Kenya",    "non-ACT", 28,    14 / 29,
  "Kenya",    "ACT",     14,    50 / 90,
  "Kenya",    "ACT",     28,    10 / 84,
  "Tanzania", "ACT",     14,    21 / 36,
  "Tanzania", "ACT",     28,    14 / 36,
  "Tanzania", "ACT-PQ",  14,     2 / 41,
  "Tanzania", "ACT-PQ",  28,     5 / 41
)

prev_cmp <- fig_prev |>
  left_join(prev_fig_sim |> select(trial, arm, time, model_typical = p_gametocytepos),
    by = c("trial", "arm", "time")
  ) |>
  left_join(table3, by = c("trial", "arm", "time"))

prev_cmp |>
  rename(
    "Trial" = trial, "Arm" = arm, "Day" = time,
    "Published fitted line (marginal)" = published_line,
    "Model typical value" = model_typical,
    "Observed, Table 3" = observed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

ggplot(prev_fig_sim, aes(time, p_gametocytepos, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = prev_cmp, aes(y = published_line), shape = 1, size = 2.5) +
  geom_point(data = table3, aes(y = observed), shape = 4, size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~trial) +
  labs(
    x = "Days since start of treatment",
    y = "Gametocyte prevalence",
    colour = "Arm",
    caption = paste(
      "Lines: model typical value. Circles: fitted lines digitised from Figures 4 and 5.",
      "Crosses: observed prevalence, Table 3."
    )
  )
```

The typical-value curves track the published lines, and every difference
points the way a logit-scale random effect moves a marginal mean: averaging
over the random effect pulls probabilities toward one half, so the
published line lies below the typical value while the prevalence is above
0.5 (Kenya non-ACT, for example 0.570 against
`r round(prev_cmp$model_typical[prev_cmp$arm == "non-ACT" & prev_cmp$time == 28], 3)`
at day 28) and above it once the prevalence has fallen below 0.5 (Kenya
ACT, 0.200 against
`r round(prev_cmp$model_typical[prev_cmp$trial == "Kenya" & prev_cmp$arm == "ACT" & prev_cmp$time == 28], 3)`
at day 28). The random-effect variance is not reported, so the marginal
curve itself cannot be recomputed.

# NCA

There is no drug concentration in these models -- the treatments enter as
arm indicators, not as doses -- so a PKNCA analysis does not apply. The
checks above (closed forms, circulation-time slopes, and the area under the
probability of carriage) take its place.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Four files for four fits.** The paper fitted each model to each trial
  separately (Methods: 'Each trial was fitted separately'), with the arms of a
  trial fitted jointly; the four files follow that structure.
* **Density-model time origin.** Table 2 reports the initial states as the
  day-3 values (S3, G3) and Figures 2-3 draw the fitted lines from day 3, so
  the density models' time zero is day 3 after the start of treatment. The
  direct drug effect on days 0-2 is not modelled; the paper folds it into G3
  and S3.
* **Unreported variances.** The density models' patient random effect on
  overall log density (`etalg3`, applied to both pools) and residual SD on
  log density (`expSd`), and the prevalence models' logit-scale patient
  random effect (`etalogitgam`), are named in the Methods but their variances
  are not reported; all three are `fixed(0)`. Simulations are typical-value.
* **Censoring.** Densities below 0.02 gametocytes/uL were treated as
  left-censored in the fit. Censoring lives in the data (for example a
  `CENS` column when estimating with nlmixr2), not in the model file.
* **Published fitted lines not reproduced.** The density lines of Figures 2-3
  are flatter and higher than the typical-value curve; the prevalence lines
  of Figures 4-5 are marginal predictions. Neither can be recomputed without
  the unreported variances (see the comparisons above).
* **Circulation times from the figure captions.** The captions give three
  significant figures (6.53, 5.04, 4.61, 0.53 days) where the Results text
  rounds to two; the caption values are used and agree with Additional
  file 1.
* **Sequestered pool S3.** Kenya non-ACT S3 = 0.0263 is the best-fitting value
  of the Additional file 1 sensitivity grid and is fixed; the Kenya ACT pool
  is fixed three natural-log units lower (Methods), coded exactly as
  `log(0.0263) - 3` (Table 2 prints 0.0013). Table 2 gives the Tanzania S3 of
  0.0013 with a confidence interval, which by its footnote marks an
  estimated value, so it is not fixed; it equals the Kenya ACT value.
* **Time to positivity in Tanzania.** Table 2 prints `1/f` = 5.60 with a
  confidence interval in the Tanzania column, but its footnote says the
  value was estimated from the Kenya data. It is estimated in the Kenya file
  and fixed in the Tanzania file.
* **Enrolment status.** The paper's `I0` is the patient's gametocyte status at
  day 0 (`GAMETOCYTE_POS_BASE`). The Table 3 footnote says every analysed
  child was gametocyte-positive at enrolment, while the Table 2 footnote
  counts 4, 12, 6 and 4 gametocyte-negative children in the four arms, and
  the day-0 points of Figures 4-5 (about 0.90, 0.89, 0.98 and 0.98) match
  neither exactly. The virtual cohort uses the Table 2 counts; the figure
  comparison uses the figures' own day-0 values.
* **New names.** The maintainers registered `TRT_ARTEMISININ` (ACT arm,
  pooling artesunate and artemether regimens), `TRT_PRIMAQUINE` and
  `GAMETOCYTE_POS_BASE` as covariates, and `gametocyte_density`,
  `gametocyte_status`, `s_gametocyteneg` and `s_gametocytepos` as states and
  outputs. The sequestered and circulating gametocyte pools are declared
  paper-specific compartments.
